newsitem.title: CHINA: China's wheat, corn market prices low in April.
newsitem.headline: China's wheat, corn market prices low in April.

text.p: China wheat prices averaged 1,690 yuan ($203) per tonne on the open market in April, down by 3.09 percent compared with 1,744 yuan per tonne in February, the Economic Daily said on Friday.
Corn prices averaged 1,110 yuan per tonne, down by 0.89 percent compared with 1,120 yuan per tonne in March and 1,150 yuan per tonne in February, it said, quoting the Zhengzhou Commodities Exchange.

The wheat price would hold at its present level due to excess supply and price falls in the international market, it said. Corn prices would rise due to price increases in the international market, it said.

In April, the average price of soybeans in the open market was 3,188 yuan per tonne, down by 0.38 percent compared with 3,200 yuan per tonne in March. The price could rise due to tight supply, it said.

Total soybean output in 1997/98 was estimated to be at 14.92 million tonnes, rising by 12 percent, with total planting area at 9.2 million hectares or up by about 10 percent compared with 1996/97, it said.

Demand for soybeans in 1997/98 was estimated to be 15.6 million tonnes, rising by 5.8 percent compared with the previous season, it said. Prices for edible oil would rise due to tight supply, it said.
